page.layout: One printed page, single text column with a woodcut headpiece above the title and a historiated initial at the start of Thesis I; faint show-through text from the reverse side in the background (not transcribed). Below the text: signature "A 2" at lower left and a catchword-like reference "4:8.&" at lower right, which is printed text in the running foot line. No marginal notes.

main_text.head: DISPUTATIO THEOLOGICA De GLORIOSA CHRISTI IN COELUM ASCENSIONE.
THESIS I.

p.i: ASCENSIO Christi in cœlum est secundus exaltationis gradus, quo Christus quadragesimo à resurrectione die, aspicientibus discipulis è terra in supremum cœlum potentiâ suæ divinitatis sublatus est, ad comparendum ibi coram facie Dei Patris pro nobis.

main_text.head: II.
main_text.p: Ad pleniorem materiæ hujus intelligentiam, ostendemus 1. Ascensionis Christi certitudinem, 2. Ascensionis subjectum, 3. Ascensionis modum, 4. Ascensionis tempus, 5. Causam, tandem ejus necessitatem & fructus.
main_text.head: III.
main_text.p: 1. Christum in cœlum ascendere debuisse, tandem verò revera ascendisse patet 1. Ex vaticinijs V. T. satis dilucidis, jam præorditur Deus per Davidem, Psal. 68: 18. 19. Currum Dei duæ sunt myriades, millia multiplicia: Dominus cum illis est, Dominus Sinai in sanctuario habitans. Ascendens in sublime, captivam fecisti captivorum multitudinem, accipiens dedisti dona hominibus, etiam rebelles habitando captivos facis. prædictioni respondit eventus, ut patet ex Eph. 4: 8. &

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse page is present throughout the background and was excluded. The initial "A" is a historiated woodcut letter, transcribed as the first letter of "ASCENSIO". Some lines in the third paragraph are partly illegible in the scan (around "jam præorditur"; the printed text reads "jam præ-" in the scan, which I could not confirm letter by letter, so it is marked as uncertain: "præorditur" [?]). The line beginning "facis." and the Ephesians reference are set in a smaller italic; the reference "4:8.&" at the foot is part of the text line.
